title: Pro-Communist And Anti-Imperialist Propaganda In Gurmukhi Seized By The French Police

S. B. REGI
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. D
Section 2, Special Branch
REPORT
February 28, 35.
Pro-Communist and Anti-Imperialist propaganda in Gurmukhi seized
by the French Police.
Made N and D.I. Ross.

I forward herewith an anti-imperialist and pro-Communist
handbill, handwritten in Gurmukhi, which was seized by the
French Police during the course of a raid on a communist base
at No. 6 Veng Bu Fang (文方), Ting Ka Loong (丁家弄), Rue
Remi, on February 19, 1935.

It will be recalled that stereotyped copies of the
abovementioned handbill in English made their appearance in
the Dixwell Road and Hongkew Districts on February 14 and
15, 1935, respectively, and that a summary of its contents
was included in the Daily Intelligence Summary of February 15.

The attached document was obtained by the undersigned
from the French Police on February 28, 1935.

D.B. Ross
D. I.

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)

（左侧批注：）
S.S. Linfoot
as advised
Eland.
28/2/35.

Gurmukhi handwriting be identified?
Were previous Red documents in
Gurmukhi, which were found, written
by the same person? What about Muller
Red case?
J.M.

DEAR BROTHERS! The massacring gun,- free of Japanese imperialism in China,
and the armament race of Japanese British and American imperialism for a
predatory war ought to awake us from slumber. We are for peace and against
predatory war but we can not enjoy the least bit of the blessing of peace
so long as we are under the enslavement, exploitation and persecution of
British Imp. & Indian Congressmen. We must fight for the peace of our own
with the national revolutionary war against British Imp. Dear Brothers, be-
cause the English Imp. oppressed us so far and no other way but revolution-
ary war can catch the complete independence of Indian country. We like no
2nd Big War but Revolutionary War. We oppose the Congressmen specially as
Gandhi because he is the devil saint of Imp-Congressmen. And we must combine
with the non-Indian poors because they want same to fight down any Imp. and
their running dogs. Brothers, by name of our Holy National Revolutionary War,
join into Kirty Party to fight down the Imp.-Congressmen! Take the revolu-
tionary war for the coming World War! Support USSR and Chinese Soviet. Re-
fuse to arrest the Chinese Kirty! Against the Japanese war to attack Inner
& Outer Mongolia, to attack USSR, for the Chinese national revolutionary war.
Against the policemen to arrest the anti-Imp. workers & peasants in Sh'ai.
Ask the equal money, boots, food and other with the English servicemen in C.
Oppose any little fine! Dismiss the bad officers and surgeons! The Chinese
Indian nations, unite against Britain, Japan and all other Imperialism!

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Communistic Literature found.

At 9.40 p.m. 15/2/35, Mrs. Robertson, (wife of
C/Insp. Robertson) brought to Honkow Charge Room,
21 handbills of a Communistic nature, which she had
found at 9.30 p.m. 15/2/35, pushed under the loosun
wood garden gate of her quarters.

An immediate search in the vicinity failed to
locate anyone that may have placed the handbills under
the gate, or any witnesses to the occurrence.

The handbills are stereotyped in English and
advocate a revolutionary war, etc, etc, and are signed
"Anti-Imperialism League in Shanghai".

D.S. Macadie, Special Branch, was informed.
Copies forwarded to Special Branch.

DSB/14/2/35

Made by......Det. Sun Pao-hwa.      Forwarded by      D.B.Ross D.I.

I forward herewith copy of a mimeographed handbill
of an anti-imperialist and pro-communist nature, dated January,
1935, written in faulty English, which purports to have emanated
from the Anti-Imperialist League in Shanghai. Fifty-three
copies of this leaflet were found by the Municipal Police
outside the wall of Dixwell Road Station on the morning of
February 14, 1935.
A brief summary of the handbill in question for
including in the Daily Intelligence Summary is attached herewith.

Sun Pao-hwa

Anti-Imperialist & Pro-Communist Propaganda

Copies of a mimeographed handbill dated January,
1935, purporting to have emanated from the Anti-Imperialist
League in Shanghai, were found by the Municipal Police
outside Dixwell Road Station during the morning of February 14.
Apart from denouncing the alleged oppression and
atrocities of the Japanese, British, and American
Imperialists, the handbill exhorts the addressees to strive
for the independence of India and to remove the enslavement,
exploitation and persecution of British Imperialists and
Indian Congressmen. Of the latter M. Gandhi is described
as the "devil saint of Imperialist congressmen." The
document concludes by urging the readers to oppose petty
fines and to demand equal treatment with the British members
of the S.M.C. as well as the dismissal of oppressive officers.
